text:
Booking an apartment in Osaka for your group? Read this before you pay. 🏠

Four people in Osaka usually choose between three options. None is always cheapest. It depends on how many nights you stay, how many bathrooms you need, and whether you want someone at a front desk.

━━━━━━━━━━
⚠️ FIRST, IS IT LEGAL?
━━━━━━━━━━

Short-term rentals in Japan need a registration or a special-zone certification, and legal hosts must record your passport at check-in.

Osaka City stopped taking new special-zone applications on 29 May 2026 and has been inspecting rentals more closely. Unlicensed listings are more likely to be cancelled at short notice.

Our 3-step check:
1️⃣ Find the registration or certification number on the listing. No number, no booking.
2️⃣ Expect a passport check. A host who never asks for ID is a warning sign.
3️⃣ Add cleaning fees and taxes for every night before you compare with hotel rooms.

━━━━━━━━━━
🏠 PRIVATE APARTMENT
━━━━━━━━━━

Good: one shared living space, a kitchen, a washing machine.
Watch: often one bathroom for four, cleaning fees, self check-in, and some have a minimum stay.

━━━━━━━━━━
🏨 APARTMENT HOTEL
━━━━━━━━━━

Good: real beds for four, a kitchenette, a laundry machine, and staff if something goes wrong.
Watch: popular with groups, so they book out early.

━━━━━━━━━━
🛏️ TWO TWIN ROOMS
━━━━━━━━━━

Good: two bathrooms, daily cleaning, easy cancellation, often right by the station.
Watch: rooms are compact and there's no common space to hang out.

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ OUR TAKE
━━━━━━━━━━

2–3 nights: two twin rooms near a station are usually the easiest.

4 nights or more: an apartment hotel often wins, because laundry and a living room start to matter.

Full comparison 👉 https://japanbystation.com/osaka-four-friends
